summary: Okanogan County summit tower built 1934 with an L-6 cab; Aircraft Warning post 1942-43; tower removed in the 1950s, cabin burned in the 1960s; footings remain.

facts.design: 72-foot pole tower with L-6 cab, built with a log cabin
facts.status_note: Tower removed in the 1950s and the cabin burned in the 1960s; WillhiteWeb photo captions show two footings at the summit
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (national forest named inconsistently across sources)

access.note: Gravel road from Chesaw Road to Summit Lake; a high-clearance vehicle can reach the summit. National Forest covers most of the mountain.

visit.trail_note: Most visitors park at Summit Lake; a high-clearance 4WD can drive to the summit, per WillhiteWeb

events.note: Road completed and tower construction started in late May 1934; register describes a 72-foot pole tower with L-6 cab and log cabin
Aircraft Warning Service station activated March 27, 1942
AWS station deactivated July 1, 1943; site reverted to Forest Service control
Register and firelookout.com say abandoned in the 1940s; the year shown stands for the decade
Tower removed in the 1950s (decade only in the sources); cabin given to the Oroville Boy Scouts
Log cabin burned in the 1960s (decade only); Willhite says only a heli-pad was left on the summit

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Weebly page names the Colville National Forest and quotes a May 1944 AWS report naming the Chelan; firelookout.com names the Okanogan; the register says only U.S. Forest Service. The story reports the disagreement.
The register gives 4,617 ft (1,407 m), matching the brief; WillhiteWeb gives 4,619 ft. Elevation is not used in the story.
The register says abandoned in the 1940s and removed in the 1950s; WillhiteWeb says discontinued in the 1940s and pulled down in the 1950s. The decades agree.

notes_for_editor: No source in the four pages names a lookout for Mount Hull. The staffing as_of 1943 marks the end of the AWS station, not a documented end of lookout service. Decade-only events use 1940, 1950 and 1960 as placeholders. The register's 2011 registration, coordinates and elevation match the brief. The national forest disagreement is unresolved and reported in the story. Confidence is medium because of the forest conflict and because the only current-condition evidence is photo captions and a 2020 visit.
